title.zh: 卷247 列傳三十四 彭而述 陆振芬 姚延著 毕振姬 方国栋 于朋举 王天鑑 越廷标
title.en: Volume 247 Biographies 34: Peng Ershu, Lu Zhenfen, Yao Yanzhu, Bi Zhenji, Fang Guodong, Yu Pengju, Wang Tianjian, Yue Tingbiao
title.raw: 卷247 列傳三十四 彭而述 陆振芬 姚延著 毕振姬 方国栋 于朋举 王天鑑 越廷标

sentences.zh: =彭而述=彭而述，字子籛，河南鄧州人。

translations.literal: =Peng Ershu= Peng Ershu, courtesy name Zihuo, was a native of Dengzhou in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ershu, styled Zihuo, came from Dengzhou in Henan.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎進士，官陽曲知縣，母憂歸。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi of the Chongzhen reign of the Ming, served as magistrate of Yangqu, and returned home upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the Chongzhen era of the Ming, held office as magistrate of Yangqu, and went home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 順治初，英親王徇湖廣，薦為提學僉事，遷永州道參議。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi, when the Prince of Ying campaigned in Huguang, Ershu was recommended as education commissioner and was transferred to assistant administrator of the Yongzhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shunzhi reign, as the Prince of Ying campaigned through Huguang, he recommended Ershu for the post of education commissioner; Ershu was later transferred to assistant administrator on the Yongzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 孔有德定湖南，薦而述授貴州巡撫，予兵三千以行。

translations.literal: When Kong Youde pacified Hunan, he recommended Ershu to be appointed governor of Guizhou and gave him three thousand troops for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: After Kong Youde brought Hunan under control, he recommended Ershu for appointment as governor of Guizhou and supplied three thousand soldiers for his expedition.

sentences.zh: 次靖州，降將陳友龍叛，圍州城，而述夜開西門出，營山下，選勁騎乘霧衝陣，賊潰且走，副將賀進才戰死。

translations.literal: When he reached Jingzhou, the surrendered general Chen Youlong rebelled and besieged the prefectural city. Ershu opened the west gate by night and went out, encamped below the mountain, selected elite cavalry to charge the enemy lines through the fog, the bandits broke and fled, and the deputy general He Jincai died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingzhou the surrendered general Chen Youlong rose in revolt and besieged the city. Ershu slipped out through the west gate by night and pitched camp below the hills, then sent picked cavalry charging through the mist; the rebels broke and fled, though Deputy Commander He Jincai fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 城兵大噪，欲與友龍合，而述拔眾退守寶慶，告有德益師，與賊相持紫陽河上。

translations.literal: The garrison soldiers raised a great clamor, wishing to join Chen Youlong; Ershu withdrew his troops to hold Baoxing, reported to Youde to send reinforcements, and faced the bandits in stalemate along the Ziyang River.
translations.idiomatic: The city troops raised an uproar and seemed ready to side with Youlong; Ershu pulled his force back to defend Baoxing, asked Youde for more troops, and faced the enemy in a stalemate along the Ziyang River.

sentences.zh: 永州陷，劾免官。

translations.literal: When Yongzhou fell, he was impeached and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongzhou was lost, he was impeached and removed from his post.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂徵水西土司安坤，而述謀曰：「烏蒙、烏撒、鎮雄、東川四府與水西為脣齒，土司隴安籓又與安氏婚媾。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui campaigned against An Kun, the native chieftain of Shuixi, Ershu advised, saying: "The four prefectures of Wumeng, Wusa, Zhenxiong, and Dongchuan are lip and teeth to Shuixi, and the native official Long Anfan is also allied by marriage with the An clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui marched against An Kun, the Shuixi chieftain, Ershu urged: "The four prefectures of Wumeng, Wusa, Zhenxiong, and Dongchuan stand with Shuixi like lip to teeth, and the tusi Long Anfan is tied to the An family by marriage as well.

sentences.zh: 今四府雖名內附，狼子野心，勢必顧惜其種類。

translations.literal: Though the four prefectures are now nominally submitted within, they have the heart of a wolf cub and will surely look after their own kind.
translations.idiomatic: Though the four prefectures now profess allegiance to the court, their hearts remain untamed; they are bound to shield their own people.

sentences.zh: 以水西之強，而安籓與四府附之，安坤未易制也。

translations.literal: With the strength of Shuixi, and Anfan and the four prefectures attached to it, An Kun will not be easy to subdue.
translations.idiomatic: Shuixi is strong, and with Anfan and the four prefectures behind it, An Kun will not be easily brought to heel.

sentences.zh: 莫如先定四府，馘安籓，然後西南可無患。

translations.literal: It would be better first to settle the four prefectures and behead Anfan; then the southwest may be free of trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Better to secure the four prefectures first and cut down Anfan; only then can the southwest be kept free of trouble.

sentences.zh: 」三桂用其策，誅安坤。

translations.literal: " Sangui adopted his plan and executed An Kun.
translations.idiomatic: " Sangui took his advice and put An Kun to death.

sentences.zh: 遷廣西右布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be right administration commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right administration commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 三桂薦為雲南左布政使，而述乞歸，三桂留之，會有詔召，遂行，出會城三十里，一夕無疾卒。

translations.literal: Sangui recommended him as left administration commissioner of Yunnan. Ershu begged to return home; Sangui detained him, but when an imperial summons arrived he set out, and thirty li beyond the provincial capital he died suddenly in one night without prior illness.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui recommended him for left administration commissioner of Yunnan. Ershu asked leave to go home; Sangui tried to keep him, but when an imperial summons came he departed, and thirty li beyond the capital he died suddenly in the night without any known illness.

sentences.zh: =陸振芬=陸振芬，字令遠，江南華亭人。

translations.literal: =Lu Zhenfen= Lu Zhenfen, courtesy name Lingyuan, was a native of Huating in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhenfen, styled Lingyuan, came from Huating in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the sixth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 時兩粵未平，廷議破格用人，即新進士中遴才除道府。

translations.literal: At that time the two Guang provinces were not yet pacified; the court discussed appointing men outside the usual rules and selecting talented new jinshi for circuit and prefectural posts.
translations.idiomatic: The two Guang provinces were still unsettled, and the court resolved to bend the rules and appoint newly minted jinshi of proven talent to circuit and prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 振芬授廣東惠潮道副使，從師南征。

translations.literal: Zhenfen was appointed vice commissioner of the Huichao circuit in Guangdong and followed the army south on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfen was made vice commissioner of the Huichao circuit in Guangdong and marched south with the expeditionary force.

sentences.zh: 是冬，克南雄。

translations.literal: That winter they captured Nanxiong.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Nanxiong was taken.

sentences.zh: 七年春，度大庾嶺，次韶州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year they crossed Dayu Ridge and halted at Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year the army crossed Dayu Ridge and encamped at Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 韶州以南望風降，進規會城，既下，振芬與總兵郭虎率師赴惠州，剿撫歸善、海豐諸寨。

translations.literal: South of Shaozhou places submitted at the mere rumor of the army; they advanced to invest the provincial capital, and after it fell Zhenfen and the commander Guo Hu led troops to Huizhou to suppress and pacify the stockades of Guishan, Haifeng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: South of Shaozhou the country submitted as the army advanced; after the capital was taken, Zhenfen and Commander Guo Hu led a force to Huizhou to subdue and win over the stockades of Guishan, Haifeng, and neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 將至，諸寨窺兵寡，出拒。

translations.literal: As they were about to arrive, the stockades, seeing how few the troops were, came out to resist.
translations.idiomatic: As the column approached, the stockades, judging the force too small, sallied out to fight.

sentences.zh: 振芬選精銳數百人繞出其旁擊之，獲一隊，諸寨皆懼。

translations.literal: Zhenfen selected several hundred elite troops to strike them from the flank, captured one band, and all the stockades were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfen picked several hundred crack troops to swing around and strike from the flank, took one band prisoner, and every stockade was shaken.

sentences.zh: 於是諭以禍福，降者踵至。

translations.literal: Thereupon he instructed them on gain and loss, and those who surrendered came one after another.
translations.idiomatic: He then lectured them on the consequences of resistance and submission, and surrenders came in one after another.

sentences.zh: 至海豐，守者抗不下。

translations.literal: At Haifeng the defenders resisted and the place would not fall.
translations.idiomatic: At Haifeng the defenders held out and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 振芬與虎駐五坡驛，他將自羊氾嶺會師合攻之，遂克其城。

translations.literal: Zhenfen and Hu encamped at Wupo Post; another general joined forces from Yangfan Ridge for a combined assault, and they then took the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfen and Hu camped at Wupo Post while another general marched from Yangfan Ridge to join the assault; the city fell.

sentences.zh: 碣石衛亦降。

translations.literal: Jieshi Guard also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Jieshi Guard surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 八年，抵潮州，上官，聯結諸鎮，檢制土官，招集流亡，簡省徭役，民始有更生之樂。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he reached Chaozhou, reported to his superiors, linked the garrisons, restrained native officials, gathered the displaced, and simplified corvée labor, so the people first knew the joy of rebirth.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he reached Chaozhou, took up his post, coordinated the garrisons, kept native officials in check, gathered refugees, and lightened corvée burdens, until the people at last felt life returning.

sentences.zh: 亂甫定，用法嚴，郡縣輒濫禁無辜。

translations.literal: The turmoil had just settled; the law was applied strictly, and prefectures and counties often imprisoned the innocent without cause.
translations.idiomatic: With the rebellion only just ended, the law was enforced harshly, and prefectures and counties often locked up innocent people at will.

sentences.zh: 振芬與屬吏約，期五十日清庶獄，囹圄為空。

translations.literal: Zhenfen agreed with his subordinate officials to clear the common prisons within fifty days, and the jails were emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfen pledged to his staff that they would clear the backlog of ordinary cases within fifty days, and the prisons were emptied.

sentences.zh: 九年，會師復平遠，總兵郝尚久故降將，陰持兩端，聞將改授水師副總兵，結山海諸寇僭立帥府。

translations.literal: In the ninth year allied forces recovered Pingyuan. The commander Hao Shangjiu, formerly a surrendered general, secretly wavered between two sides; hearing that he was to be reassigned as deputy commander of the naval forces, he joined the mountain and sea bandits in arrogantly establishing a command headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year allied columns recovered Pingyuan. Commander Hao Shangjiu, once a surrendered Ming officer, had long played both sides; when he learned he was to be transferred to deputy naval commander, he joined coastal and mountain rebels in setting up a rival headquarters.

sentences.zh: 振芬牒大吏策弭變，不應。

translations.literal: Zhenfen memorialized the high officials with a plan to quell the disturbance, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfen sent the senior authorities a memorandum outlining how to head off the revolt, but they did not act.

sentences.zh: 十年春，尚久自署新泰侯，舉兵圍道署。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year Shangjiu styled himself Marquis of Xintai, raised troops, and besieged the circuit yamen.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the tenth year Shangjiu declared himself Marquis of Xintai, took up arms, and besieged the circuit headquarters.

sentences.zh: 振芬諭以大義，不從，使告變。

translations.literal: Zhenfen admonished him with the greater principle of loyalty, but Shangjiu would not obey; Zhenfen sent word of the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfen appealed to him on grounds of loyalty, but Shangjiu refused to listen, so he sent word of the uprising.

sentences.zh: 秋，固山兵至，振芬約為內應，引外兵入，誅尚久。

translations.literal: In autumn the garrison troops arrived; Zhenfen arranged to act as inner support, led the outside troops in, and executed Shangjiu.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the banner garrison arrived; Zhenfen arranged an inside rendezvous, guided the relief force in, and had Shangjiu put to death.

sentences.zh: 事平，引疾歸里。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he pleaded illness and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, he cited illness and retired to his home.

sentences.zh: 家居四十年乃卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home forty years before he died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement forty years before he died.

sentences.zh: =姚延著=姚延著，字象懸，浙江烏程人。

translations.literal: =Yao Yanzhu= Yao Yanzhu, courtesy name Xiangxuan, was a native of Wucheng in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yanzhu, styled Xiangxuan, came from Wucheng in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士，除廣西慶遠知府。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the sixth year of Shunzhi and was appointed prefect of Qingyuan in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the sixth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed prefect of Qingyuan in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 從師南征，調柳州，有守禦功，又調平樂。

translations.literal: He followed the army south on campaign, was transferred to Liuzhou where he had merit in defense, and was again transferred to Pingle.
translations.idiomatic: He marched south with the army, was transferred to Liuzhou where he distinguished himself in defense, and was then moved to Pingle.

sentences.zh: 遷廣東嶺南道副使，撫僮寨，擢江南按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commissioner of the Lingnan circuit in Guangdong, pacified Zhuang stockades, and was elevated to provincial surveillance commissioner of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice commissioner of the Lingnan circuit in Guangdong, pacified Zhuang stockades, and was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 十六年，鄭成功內犯，陷鎮江，入攻江寧。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Zheng Chenggong invaded inland, took Zhenjiang, and advanced to attack Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Zheng Chenggong struck inland, captured Zhenjiang, and pressed the attack on Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 延著佐總督郎廷佐繕守備，安輯危城，閭閻不擾。

translations.literal: Yanzhu assisted Governor Lang Tingzuo in preparing defenses, steadied the endangered city, and the neighborhoods were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhu helped Governor Lang Tingzuo organize the defenses, steadied the beleaguered city, and kept the streets calm.

sentences.zh: 民間時有羊尾黨，事發，株連數百人。

translations.literal: Among the people there was at times the Yangwei faction; when the affair broke, several hundred were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: A faction known as the Yangwei clique surfaced among the people; when the case broke, several hundred were dragged in.

sentences.zh: 延著謂廷佐曰：「寇在門，不可興大獄、搖人心。

translations.literal: Yanzhu said to Tingzuo: "The bandits are at the gate; one must not launch a great trial and shake the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhu told Tingzuo, "The enemy is at the gates; we must not open a sweeping prosecution and unsettle the populace.

sentences.zh: 」獄乃解。

translations.literal: " The case was then dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: " The case was dropped.

sentences.zh: 當事急，人多疑貳，民間有宿怨，輒誣以通敵。

translations.literal: In the emergency many were suspected of wavering loyalty; where old grudges existed among the people, others were readily accused of communicating with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the crisis many were suspected of divided loyalties, and private feuds often ended in accusations of collusion with the enemy.

sentences.zh: 延著嚴治反坐，多所全活。

translations.literal: Yanzhu strictly punished false accusation and thereby saved many lives.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhu punished malicious denunciation severely and thereby spared many lives.

sentences.zh: 城民有升高而望者，邏者執之，總管喀喀木以為敵諜，延著力爭，得不死。

translations.literal: A city resident climbed high to look out; patrolmen seized him, and Commander Kekemu took him for an enemy spy; Yanzhu argued strenuously and he was not put to death.
translations.idiomatic: When a townsman climbed somewhere high to look out, patrolmen seized him and Commander Kekemu judged him a spy; Yanzhu argued hard and saved his life.

sentences.zh: 喀喀木部兵擾城市，延著捕得械斃之。

translations.literal: Troops under Kekemu harassed the city; Yanzhu captured the offenders and had them executed by military law.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers under Kekemu were molesting the city; Yanzhu seized the culprits and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 吏卒私掠被難婦女，延著親駐江乾，召其家，遣還者一千七百人，以此忤喀喀木。

translations.literal: Clerks and soldiers privately seized women caught in the disaster; Yanzhu personally stationed himself on the riverbank, summoned their families, and sent back one thousand seven hundred persons, thereby offending Kekemu.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks and soldiers were seizing women from distressed families; Yanzhu went in person to the riverbank, summoned their kin, and sent home seventeen hundred people, which earned Kekemu's enmity.

sentences.zh: 事定敘功，擢河南左布政使。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled merits were recorded and he was promoted to left administration commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After the crisis he was rewarded for merit and promoted to left administration commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 旋以憂歸，而金壇獄起。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he returned home on bereavement, and the Jintan case arose.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went home to mourn, and then the Jintan case erupted.

sentences.zh: 鎮江之陷也，屬縣戒嚴。

translations.literal: When Zhenjiang fell, the subordinate counties were placed under strict guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenjiang fell, the surrounding counties went on alert.

sentences.zh: 金壇知縣任體坤集縣中士大夫王重、袁大受等謀遣諸生十輩詣鎮江乞緩兵。

translations.literal: The Jintan magistrate Ren Tikun gathered the local gentry Wang Chong, Yuan Dashou, and others to plan sending ten batches of students to Zhenjiang to beg for a truce.
translations.idiomatic: Jintan's magistrate Ren Tikun gathered local notables Wang Chong, Yuan Dashou, and others to send ten groups of students to Zhenjiang to plead for a ceasefire.

sentences.zh: 丹徒亂民王再興兵起，復令書吏、耆民數十人送款，盡竊庫帑以遁。

translations.literal: Wang Zai, a rebel of Dantu, raised troops; Tikun again ordered several dozen clerks and elders to submit terms of surrender, and they stole the entire treasury and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dantu rebel Wang Zai rose in arms, Tikun again sent dozens of clerks and elders to offer surrender, and they plundered the treasury and fled.

sentences.zh: 喀喀木等擊敗成功，體坤乃復至縣，賂重、大受謁大吏，謂士民送款，冀掩棄城罪。

translations.literal: Kekemu and others defeated Chenggong; Tikun then returned to the county, bribed Chong and Dashou to visit the high officials, and claimed that gentry and people had submitted, hoping to cover the crime of abandoning the city.
translations.idiomatic: After Kekemu and others routed Chenggong, Tikun returned to the county and bribed Chong and Dashou to lobby the senior authorities, claiming the gentry had surrendered in order to hide his guilt for abandoning the city.

sentences.zh: 重、大受居鄉多不法，為諸生所撓。

translations.literal: Chong and Dashou had long committed many unlawful acts in their home districts and were thwarted by the students.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and Dashou had long bullied the countryside and had been checked by the local students.

sentences.zh: 至是欲以叛坐諸生，泄私怨，列姓名以上。

translations.literal: Now they wished to convict the students of rebellion to vent private grudges and submitted a list of names.
translations.idiomatic: Now they sought to charge the students with treason to settle old scores and submitted a roll of names.

sentences.zh: 巡按馬勝聲疏聞，下廷佐令延著鞫其獄。

translations.literal: The touring censor Ma Shengsheng memorialized the throne; the case was sent down to Tingzuo ordering Yanzhu to try it.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Censor Ma Shengsheng reported the matter, and the court ordered Tingzuo to have Yanzhu hear the case.

sentences.zh: 延著縶縣吏李鍾秀，訊得實，欲但坐體坤，餘皆減罪。

translations.literal: Yanzhu arrested the county clerk Li Zhongxiu, examined him and learned the truth, and wished to punish only Tikun while reducing the offenses of the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhu detained county clerk Li Zhongxiu, learned the facts, and sought to punish only Tikun while mitigating the charges against the others.

sentences.zh: 大受騰書京師為蜚語，欲並陷延著，御史馮班發其狀。

translations.literal: Dashou sent letters to the capital spreading rumors, intending to implicate Yanzhu as well; Censor Feng Ban exposed his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou sent inflammatory letters to the capital hoping to drag Yanzhu down as well, but Censor Feng Ban exposed his scheme.

sentences.zh: 時侍郎尼滿奉詔勘提督馬逢知獄，命即訊，乃坐重、大受及諸士大夫集議者。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Minister Niman was ordered by imperial edict to investigate the case of Governor-General Ma Fengzhi and was commanded to try this case at once; he then convicted Chong, Dashou, and the gentry who had met in council.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Niman had been sent to investigate Governor-General Ma Fengzhi and was ordered to take this case immediately; he convicted Chong, Dashou, and the gentry who had met to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 諸生及書吏、耆民送款者皆斬，體坤以被逼迫減為絞。

translations.literal: The students and the clerks and elders who had submitted terms were all beheaded; Tikun, on the ground of coercion, had his sentence reduced to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: The students and the clerks and elders who had offered surrender were all beheaded; Tikun, as one who had acted under duress, was sentenced to strangulation instead.

sentences.zh: 巡按何可化又疏劾延著讞從叛罪人史記青、管得勝傅輕比，又有王天福、韓王錫並縱不擬罪，與金壇獄並論，亦坐絞。

translations.literal: The touring censor He Kehua again memorialized impeaching Yanzhu for judging the rebel accomplices Shi Jiqing and Guan Desheng too lightly, and also for releasing Wang Tianfu and Han Wangxi without sentencing; together with the Jintan case he too was sentenced to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Censor He Kehua impeached Yanzhu again for treating rebel associates Shi Jiqing and Guan Desheng too leniently and for releasing Wang Tianfu and Han Wangxi without punishment; tried together with the Jintan affair, Yanzhu too was sentenced to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 時喀喀木主軍事，新破敵，尤威重，素不慊於延著。

translations.literal: At that time Kekemu directed military affairs, had newly defeated the enemy, and was especially formidable; he had long been displeased with Yanzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Kekemu then held military command, had just broken the enemy, and wielded exceptional power; he had long borne a grudge against Yanzhu.

sentences.zh: 民間謂延著之死，喀喀木實主之。

translations.literal: Among the people it was said that in Yanzhu's death Kekemu was in fact the prime mover.
translations.idiomatic: Popular opinion held that Kekemu was really behind Yanzhu's execution.

sentences.zh: 就刑日，江寧為罷市，士民哭踴。

translations.literal: On the day of execution Jiangning closed its markets; gentry and people wept and stamped in grief.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he was executed the markets of Jiangning closed; scholars and commoners wept and stamped in mourning.

sentences.zh: 喪歸，數百里祭奠不絕，建祠雞鳴山下私祀焉。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned, for several hundred li offerings of mourning did not cease; a shrine was built below Jiming Hill for private sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: As his coffin was borne home, mourners lined the route for hundreds of li; a shrine was raised below Jiming Hill where the people worshipped him privately.

sentences.zh: 子淳燾，康熙六年進士，授內閣中書舍人。

translations.literal: His son Chun'ao was a jinshi in the sixth year of Kangxi and was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chun'ao, a jinshi of the sixth year of Kangxi, was appointed a secretarial draftsman in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 伏闕上書為延著訟冤。

translations.literal: He prostrated himself before the palace gate and submitted a memorial to plead Yanzhu's innocence.
translations.idiomatic: He knelt before the palace gate and memorialized the throne to clear his father's name.

sentences.zh: 累擢湖廣提學道僉事，坐事罷，未行，值叛卒夏逢龍之亂，誓死不為屈。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to education commissioner of the Huguang circuit, was dismissed for an offense before he could take up the post, and when the mutinous soldier Xia Fenglong rebelled he vowed to die rather than submit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to education commissioner on the Huguang circuit, was dismissed for an offense before he could take up the post, and when the mutineer Xia Fenglong rebelled he swore he would die rather than yield.

sentences.zh: 事聞，复官，授岳常澧道副使。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, his office was restored and he was appointed vice commissioner of the Yuechangli circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court his office was restored and he was made vice commissioner of the Yuechangli circuit.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: =畢振姬=畢振姬，字亮四，山西高平人。

translations.literal: =Bi Zhenji= Bi Zhenji, courtesy name Liangsi, was a native of Gaoping in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zhenji, styled Liangsi, came from Gaoping in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 順治三年進士，授平陽教授。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the third year of Shunzhi and was appointed instructor at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed instructor at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 入為國子監助教，累遷刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered service as an assistant instructor in the Directorate of Education and was repeatedly promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Directorate of Education as an assistant instructor and rose step by step to vice director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 曹事暇，獨坐陋室，布被瓦盆，讀書不稍倦。

translations.literal: In his spare time from office duties he sat alone in a humble room with a cloth quilt and earthen bowl, reading without the slightest weariness.
translations.idiomatic: In whatever spare hours his duties allowed he sat alone in a plain room with only a cotton quilt and clay bowl, reading without flagging.

sentences.zh: 十年，出為山東濟南道參議。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he went out to serve as assistant administrator of the Jinan circuit in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was posted as assistant administrator of the Jinan circuit in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，流民踞山谷為盜，振姬晝夜馳三百里往諭之，悉就撫，全活者七​​千餘人。

translations.literal: In a year of drought, displaced people occupied the mountain valleys as bandits; Zhenji rode day and night three hundred li to instruct them, and all submitted to pacification; more than seven thousand lives were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought refugees had turned bandit in the hills; Zhenji rode three hundred li day and night to reason with them, and all accepted pacification, sparing more than seven thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 泰山香稅，歲羨餘七千金，例充公使錢，振姬悉以佐餉。

translations.literal: The incense tax of Mount Tai yielded a surplus of seven thousand taels each year, which by regulation went to public envoy funds; Zhenji devoted it all to supplement rations.
translations.idiomatic: The Mount Tai incense tax produced an annual surplus of seven thousand taels, normally reserved for official missions; Zhenji applied the whole sum to army provisions.

sentences.zh: 調廣東驛傳道僉事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be commissioner of the courier circuit in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to commissioner of the courier service circuit in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 時三籓使命往來絡繹，胥吏乘以私派折價，民苦之，振姬一繩以法，閱數月，減船數百，減​​費七萬有奇。

translations.literal: At that time missions of the Three Feudatories came and went incessantly; clerks took the opportunity for private levies and discount extortion, to the people's distress; Zhenji applied the law uniformly, and within several months reduced boats by several hundred and cut costs by more than seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: With the Three Feudatories' envoys constantly on the road, clerks imposed private surcharges and shaved payments, burdening the people; Zhenji held everyone to the law, and within months cut several hundred boats from service and saved more than seventy thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 調浙江金衢嚴道參政，擢廣西按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administration commissioner of the Jinquyan circuit in Zhejiang and was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to administration commissioner of the Jinquyan circuit in Zhejiang and then promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 所至以廉能聞。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he was known for integrity and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Every post he held won him a reputation for integrity and competence.

sentences.zh: 遷湖廣布政使，乞病歸。

translations.literal: He was promoted to administration commissioner of Huguang and begged leave on grounds of illness to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to administration commissioner of Huguang, then asked leave on grounds of illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，詔舉博學鴻儒，左都御史魏裔介、副都御史劉楗疏薦之。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign an edict called for recommending erudite scholars; the left censor-in-chief Wei Yijie and the vice censor-in-chief Liu Jian memorialized recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kangxi era an edict summoned men of broad learning; Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie and Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Jian both recommended him.

sentences.zh: 十八年，命廷臣舉清廉吏，裔介复疏言：「振姬清操絕世，才略過人。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the court ordered ministers to recommend incorrupt officials; Yijie again memorialized, saying: "Zhenji's pure conduct is unmatched in the age, and his talent and strategy surpass others.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the throne ordered the bureaucracy to nominate incorrupt officials; Yijie memorialized again: "Zhenji's integrity is unrivaled and his talent exceptional.

sentences.zh: 請告十餘年，躬耕百畝，讀書不輟。

translations.literal: For more than ten years since requesting leave he has personally farmed a hundred mu and never ceased reading.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years since he left office he has farmed a hundred mu with his own hands and never stopped his studies.

sentences.zh: 」楗亦言：「振姬居官不染一塵。

translations.literal: " Jian also said: "In office Zhenji was not stained by a speck of dust.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian added, "In office Zhenji never took a tainted coin.

sentences.zh: 歸日一僕一馬，了無長物，真學行兼優之人。

translations.literal: On returning home he had one servant and one horse and utterly lacked accumulated goods; he is truly a man of combined learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: On retiring he owned only one servant and one horse and nothing more—a man whose learning and conduct are equally exemplary.

sentences.zh: 」下部議，以振姬老，置勿用。

translations.literal: " The matter was sent to the ministries for discussion; because Zhenji was old, he was set aside and not employed.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministries deliberated and, on grounds of age, set the nomination aside.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long after.

sentences.zh: =方國棟=方國棟，字幹霄，順天宛平人。

translations.literal: =Fang Guodong= Fang Guodong, courtesy name Ganxiao, was a native of Wanping in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guodong, styled Ganxiao, came from Wanping in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 順治三年舉人，授蠡縣教諭。

translations.literal: He was a provincial graduate in the third year of Shunzhi and was appointed instructor of Li County.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate of the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed instructor of Li County.

sentences.zh: 入為國子監助教，累擢至刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He entered as an assistant instructor in the Directorate of Education and was repeatedly promoted to director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Directorate of Education as an assistant instructor and rose to director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 十六年，出為廣東海北道僉事。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he went out to serve as commissioner of the Haibei circuit in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was posted as commissioner of the Haibei circuit in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 海寇鄧耀居島中，時出剽掠。

translations.literal: The sea bandit Deng Yao dwelt on an island and often came out to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: The pirate Deng Yao held an island base and raided the coast at will.

sentences.zh: 國棟以三千人分五道進剿，檄鄰道出兵扼要隘，擒耀，解散餘黨。

translations.literal: Guodong led three thousand men in five columns to advance and suppress them, ordered neighboring circuits to send troops to hold key passes, captured Yao, and dispersed the remaining followers.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong led three thousand men in five columns against him, called on neighboring circuits to block the passes, captured Yao, and broke up the remnant bands.

sentences.zh: 事平，雷、廉兩部諸富人為賊所誣，械系者眾，國棟察其冤，為辨雪。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, many wealthy men of the Lei and Lian departments had been slandered by the bandits and were shackled in large numbers; Guodong perceived their innocence and cleared them.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign many wealthy men in Leizhou and Lianzhou had been framed by the pirates and thrown into chains; Guodong saw they were innocent and secured their release.

sentences.zh: 諸富人裒千金為報，國棟曰：「吾憫若無辜，柰何污我？

translations.literal: The wealthy men pooled a thousand taels in gratitude; Guodong said: "I pity your innocence—why would you stain me?
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy men pooled a thousand taels to thank him; Guodong said, "I pitied your innocence—why would you try to bribe me?

sentences.zh: 」卻之。

translations.literal: " He refused it.
translations.idiomatic: " He turned the gift away.

sentences.zh: 遷山西寧武道參議。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be assistant administrator of the Ningwu circuit in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to assistant administrator of the Ningwu circuit in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年裁缺，改江南蘇松常道參議。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi his post was abolished; he was reassigned as assistant administrator of the Susongchang circuit in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: When his post was abolished in the sixth year of Kangxi, he was reassigned as assistant administrator of the Susongchang circuit in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 太湖堤岸傾圮，率吏民修葺，修沿海墩台及吳淞、劉河兩徬，工費不擾民。

translations.literal: The dikes of Lake Tai collapsed; he led officials and people to repair them, restored coastal watch towers and the two embankments of Wusong and Liuhe, and the cost of labor did not trouble the people.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taihu dikes gave way he led officials and commoners in repairs, rebuilt coastal watchtowers and the Wusong and Liuhe embankments, and kept the labor levies from burdening the people.

sentences.zh: 師下閩、粵，徵調旁午，國棟一意與民休息，每遇急徵，從容部署。

translations.literal: As the army advanced into Fujian and Guangdong, requisitions came in rapid succession; Guodong was wholly intent on letting the people rest, and whenever urgent levies arrived he deployed resources with calm deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial forces marched into Fujian and Guangdong, requisitions poured in without pause; Guodong made easing the people's burdens his sole aim and met every urgent levy with calm, orderly arrangements.

sentences.zh: 芻茭糧糗，預儲以待，軍興無乏，閭左晏然。

translations.literal: Fodder and grain rations were stored in advance; when the army mobilized nothing was lacking, and the neighborhoods were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Fodder and grain were stockpiled ahead of time, so the armies never went short and the neighborhoods stayed at peace.

sentences.zh: 戒屬吏無朘民，郡縣稍稍知斂戢，不敢事剝削。

translations.literal: He warned his subordinates not to squeeze the people; prefectures and counties gradually learned restraint and did not dare to exploit them.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade his staff to squeeze the people, and prefectures and counties gradually learned restraint and ceased their extortions.

sentences.zh: 連歲用兵，度支不給，詔各省籌裕餉之策。

translations.literal: War continued year after year and the treasury could not meet expenses; an edict ordered each province to devise measures to enlarge military funds.
translations.idiomatic: Years of warfare had emptied the treasury, and the throne ordered each province to propose ways to enlarge military revenue.

sentences.zh: 國棟言：「古今生財之說，開與節二者而已。

translations.literal: Guodong said: "From ancient times to the present, theories of enriching the state come down to only two things: opening sources and practicing economy.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong argued: "From antiquity to the present, enriching the state comes down to only two things: opening new revenue and practicing economy.

sentences.zh: 議開於今日，已無可加，當議節，自朝廷始。

translations.literal: To discuss opening sources today, there is nothing more to add; one should discuss economy, beginning with the court itself.
translations.idiomatic: As for opening new sources today, there is nothing left to add; we should discuss economy, and it should begin at court.

sentences.zh: 舊制，江南歲市布五萬匹供宮府賚予，宜可罷，歲省帑金三萬。

translations.literal: By old regulation Jiangnan each year purchased fifty thousand bolts of cloth for palace gifts and grants; this might well be abolished, saving thirty thousand taels from the treasury each year.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system Jiangnan bought fifty thousand bolts of cloth yearly for palace gifts; abolishing it would save thirty thousand taels a year.

sentences.zh: 」議上，報可，滿洲兵駐防蘇州，議築營舍於王府基，當城中。

translations.literal: " The proposal was submitted and approved. Manchu troops were garrisoned at Suzhou; it was proposed to build barracks on the site of a princely mansion in the center of the city.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved. When Manchu troops were garrisoned at Suzhou, officials proposed building barracks on a former princely mansion site in the heart of the city.

sentences.zh: 國棟以兵民雜居難久安，持不可，乃改營南城隙地，民便之。

translations.literal: Guodong held that soldiers and civilians living mixed together could not long remain secure and firmly opposed it; barracks were then placed on vacant land in the southern city, to the people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong argued that soldiers and civilians could not live mixed together for long and firmly opposed the plan; the barracks were moved to vacant land in the southern city, to the people's relief.

sentences.zh: 宜興善權山中寺僧與豪族爭地，聚眾焚寺殺僧，知縣告亂，大吏將發兵。

translations.literal: At Shanchuan in Yixing, monks of a mountain temple disputed land with a powerful clan; they gathered a crowd, burned the temple, and killed monks; the magistrate reported a rebellion and the high officials were about to send troops.
translations.idiomatic: At Shanchuan in Yixing, temple monks disputed land with a powerful clan; the crowd burned the temple and killed monks. The magistrate reported rebellion and senior officials prepared to send troops.

sentences.zh: 國棟單騎馳往，得首禍寘法，餘無所問。

translations.literal: Guodong rode alone in haste, seized the chief culprits and punished them by law, and questioned no one else.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong rode out alone, seized the ringleaders and punished them, and questioned no one else.

sentences.zh: 吳俗健訟，喜投缿告密，國棟輒不問，即有所案，亦從寬。

translations.literal: The Wu region was fond of litigation and liked to drop accusations in complaint boxes; Guodong routinely paid no heed, and even when there were cases he was lenient.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou folk were quick to sue and fond of anonymous denunciation; Guodong routinely ignored such complaints, and even when cases arose he judged leniently.

sentences.zh: 馭吏嚴，而拊循士民具有恩意。

translations.literal: He was strict in controlling officials, yet in comforting gentry and commoners he showed real kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled his staff strictly yet treated scholars and commoners with genuine kindness.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year.

sentences.zh: 吳民思之，建祠虎丘山麓以祀。

translations.literal: The people of Wu missed him and built a shrine at the foot of Tiger Hill to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu missed him and raised a shrine at the foot of Tiger Hill in his honor.

sentences.zh: =於朋舉=於朋舉，字襄子，江南金壇人。

translations.literal: =Yu Pengju= Yu Pengju, courtesy name Xiangzi, was a native of Jintan in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Pengju, styled Xiangzi, came from Jintan in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士，改庶吉士，散館授檢討。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the sixth year of Shunzhi, was made a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and upon leaving the academy was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the sixth year of Shunzhi, he entered the Hanlin as a bachelor and, after completing his academy term, was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 十二年，出為河南睢陳道副使，政不擾民。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he went out to serve as vice commissioner of the Suichen circuit in Henan; his administration did not trouble the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was posted as vice commissioner of the Suichen circuit in Henan, governing without harassing the people.

sentences.zh: 郾城盜殺縣官而逸，士民洶洶，謂城將受屠。

translations.literal: Bandits at Yancheng killed the county magistrate and fled; gentry and people were in an uproar, saying the city would be put to the sword.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits at Yancheng killed the magistrate and fled; gentry and townsfolk were in an uproar, fearing the city would be massacred.

sentences.zh: 朋舉馳至，撫諭毋恐。

translations.literal: Pengju rode there in haste and comforted them, telling them not to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Pengju galloped there and reassured them not to panic.

sentences.zh: 營將以兵至，拒不使入城。

translations.literal: A garrison commander was bringing troops; Pengju refused to let them enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: When a garrison commander marched up with troops, Pengju refused to let them enter the city.

sentences.zh: 大吏召朋舉詰責，對曰：「郾城令，朋舉婦翁也。

translations.literal: The high official summoned Pengju to rebuke him; he replied: "The magistrate of Yancheng is Pengju's father-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: A senior official summoned Pengju to rebuke him; he replied, "The magistrate of Yancheng was my father-in-law.

sentences.zh: 豈不欲甘心是盜？

translations.literal: Would I not wish to have my fill of vengeance on those bandits?
translations.idiomatic: Do you think I do not want those bandits punished?

sentences.zh: 獨柰何苦良民！

translations.literal: Only why must innocent people suffer?
translations.idiomatic: But why should innocent people suffer for it?

sentences.zh: 」大吏悟，止兵，亦得盜正其罪。

translations.literal: " The high official understood, halted the troops, and the bandits were also brought to justice.
translations.idiomatic: " The official understood, halted the troops, and the bandits were still brought to justice.

sentences.zh: 遷福建福寧道參政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be administration commissioner of the Funing circuit in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to administration commissioner of the Funing circuit in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 興化瀕海，鎮將所部皆群盜受撫者。

translations.literal: Xinghua bordered the sea; the troops under the garrison commander were all bandit bands that had accepted pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Xinghua lay on the coast; the garrison commander's troops were all former bandits who had accepted pacification.

sentences.zh: 有材官辱張氏僕，張氏以告。

translations.literal: An officer insulted a servant of the Zhang family; the Zhangs reported it.
translations.idiomatic: An officer insulted a servant of the Zhang household, and the Zhangs complained.

sentences.zh: 鎮將撻材官，部卒大譁，毀張氏之室，欲劫鎮將為亂。

translations.literal: The garrison commander flogged the officer; the troops raised a great clamor, wrecked the Zhang residence, and wished to seize the commander and rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The commander had the officer flogged; the troops raised an uproar, wrecked the Zhang house, and tried to seize the commander and mutiny.

sentences.zh: 鎮將避去，則縊被撻者寘張氏，謂其僕殺之。

translations.literal: The commander fled; they then hanged the man who had been flogged and placed him at the Zhang house, claiming the Zhang servant had killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The commander fled; they hanged the flogged man and left the body at the Zhang house, claiming a Zhang servant had killed him.

sentences.zh: 朋舉甫到官，廉得首惡，猝縛至，集文武吏會鞫，健兒帶刀環立瞋視。

translations.literal: Pengju had just taken office; he investigated and found the chief culprits, seized them suddenly, gathered civil and military officials for a joint trial, while braves with swords stood in a ring glaring.
translations.idiomatic: Pengju had just taken office; he identified the ringleaders, seized them at once, and convened civil and military officials for a joint trial while armed braves ringed the hall, glaring.

sentences.zh: 朋舉從容曰：「若曹幹軍法，罪重。

translations.literal: Pengju said calmly: "You have violated military law; the offense is grave.
translations.idiomatic: Pengju said calmly, "You have violated military law—a grave offense.

sentences.zh: 念若曹約束無素，但用殺人律，罪有專屬。

translations.literal: Considering that you have never been well disciplined, I will apply only the statute on homicide; the crime has its specific bearer.
translations.idiomatic: But considering your lack of discipline, I will apply only the homicide statute—the guilty party must be identified.

sentences.zh: 」眾乃泥首，言殺人者為張氏僕。

translations.literal: " The crowd then pressed their foreheads to the ground and said the killer was the Zhang servant.
translations.idiomatic: " The men then kowtowed and named the Zhang servant as the killer.

sentences.zh: 朋舉曰：「若曹氣焰何等，彼能於千百健兒中奪一人縊之耶？

translations.literal: Pengju said: "What sort of spirit do you have—could he, among a thousand braves, seize one man and hang him?
translations.idiomatic: Pengju said, "With your numbers and ferocity, could a servant really seize one man from among a thousand braves and hang him?

sentences.zh: 」召訊證者，俱吐實，誅三人而事定。

translations.literal: " He summoned witnesses for examination; all told the truth; three were executed and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: " He summoned witnesses; all confessed; three were executed and the affair was settled.

sentences.zh: 泉州提督剿海盜，盜逸入興化界，鎮將獲數百人。

translations.literal: The Quanzhou provincial commander suppressed sea pirates; the pirates fled into the Xinghua border and the garrison commander captured several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial commander of Quanzhou pursued sea pirates; the pirates fled into Xinghua territory and the garrison commander seized several hundred.

sentences.zh: 朋舉視其嘗薙發者，曰：「此良民被陷，當宥。

translations.literal: Pengju looked at those who had once shaved their heads and said: "These are innocent people who were trapped; they should be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Pengju looked at those who had once shaved their heads in the Qing style and said, "These are innocent people caught up in the affair—they should be spared.

sentences.zh: 」有年少者，曰：「童穉何知，又當宥。

translations.literal: " Among them were youths; he said: "What do children know—they too should be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: " Seeing youths among them, he said, "Children know nothing of such matters—they too should be spared.

sentences.zh: 」全活甚眾。

translations.literal: " A great many lives were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: " A great many lives were spared.

sentences.zh: 鄭成功屯廈門，與漳州隔海相望。

translations.literal: Zheng Chenggong was encamped at Xiamen, facing Zhangzhou across the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chenggong held Xiamen, facing Zhangzhou across the strait.

sentences.zh: 固山額真駐會城，遣兵戍漳州，番代歲四易，民苦供役。

translations.literal: The garrison commander was stationed at the provincial capital and sent troops to garrison Zhangzhou; rotations changed four times a year, and the people suffered from supplying them.
translations.idiomatic: The banner garrison commander at the provincial capital posted troops to Zhangzhou; reliefs rotated four times a year, and the people groaned under the levies.

sentences.zh: 朋舉請駐防無屢更，不許；

translations.literal: Pengju requested that the garrison not be rotated so often; this was not granted;
translations.idiomatic: Pengju asked that the garrison not be rotated so often; the request was denied;

sentences.zh: 固請展其期，歲再易，民稍蘇息。

translations.literal: he firmly begged to extend the term to two rotations a year, and the people gradually recovered ease.
translations.idiomatic: he pressed hard to extend the rotation period to twice a year, and the people gradually found relief.

sentences.zh: 擢四川按察使、山東右布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Sichuan and right administration commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Sichuan and right administration commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 起授湖南布政使。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed administration commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning, he was appointed administration commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 上官，見胥吏至數百，曰：「兵初罷，民方重困。

translations.literal: Upon taking office he saw clerks numbering in the hundreds and said: "The troops have just been stood down and the people are still in deep distress.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he found hundreds of clerks and said, "The armies have only just stood down and the people are still in deep distress.

sentences.zh: 此曹鮮衣美食，縱橫市井間，何所​​取諸？

translations.literal: These fellows wear fresh clothes and eat fine food, swaggering through the markets—where do they get it?
translations.idiomatic: Yet these fellows dress well and eat well, swaggering through the markets—where does it all come from?

sentences.zh: 」汰其十九，擇謹願者，取足供文書而已。

translations.literal: " He dismissed nineteen out of twenty, chose the diligent and honest, and kept only enough to handle documents.
translations.idiomatic: " He dismissed nine out of ten, kept only the diligent and honest, and retained just enough staff to handle paperwork.

sentences.zh: 數為大吏言地方利病，有司賢不肖積與之忤，被劾鐫級，未行，而大吏以貪敗。

translations.literal: He repeatedly told the high officials of local benefits and harms; officials worthy and unworthy accumulated grievances against him; he was impeached and demoted in rank; before he could depart, the high official was ruined for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly reported local abuses to senior officials; worthy and unworthy magistrates alike resented him; he was impeached and demoted before he could leave, and the senior official who had moved against him was soon ruined for corruption.

sentences.zh: 士民惜之。

translations.literal: Gentry and people regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and commoners mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long after.

sentences.zh: =王天鑑=王天鑑，字近微，直隸萬全人。

translations.literal: =Wang Tianjian= Wang Tianjian, courtesy name Jinwei, was a native of Wanquan in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tianjian, styled Jinwei, came from Wanquan in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 順治三年進士，授山東恩縣知縣。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the third year of Shunzhi and was appointed magistrate of En County in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed magistrate of En County in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 縣接直隸界，自明季為盜藪，嘗一歲七被寇。

translations.literal: The county bordered Zhili; since the late Ming it had been a bandit lair and once suffered seven raids in a single year.
translations.idiomatic: The county bordered Zhili and had been a bandit haven since the late Ming; one year it was raided seven times.

sentences.zh: 天鑑上官，諭父老曰：「往歲寇至，縣輒不守，由人無固志。

translations.literal: When Tianjian took office he told the elders: "In past years when bandits came the county always failed to hold, because people had no firm will.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Tianjian told the elders, "In past years when bandits came the county always fell because the people had no firm will.

sentences.zh: 自今勿復逃，視知縣所向。

translations.literal: From now on do not flee again; watch where your magistrate goes.
translations.idiomatic: From now on do not flee—watch where your magistrate goes.

sentences.zh: 」俄而寇大至，天鑑坐城上，從容指揮，寇疑有伏，逡巡去。

translations.literal: " Soon bandits came in force; Tianjian sat on the city wall and directed affairs calmly; the bandits suspected an ambush and withdrew hesitantly.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon bandits came in force; Tianjian sat on the wall and directed the defense calmly; the bandits suspected an ambush and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 於是葺樓櫓，治城隍，嚴候望，時巡徼，守具大備。

translations.literal: Thereupon he repaired towers and battlements, restored the moat and walls, tightened watch posts, patrolled regularly, and made defenses fully ready.
translations.idiomatic: He then repaired towers and battlements, restored the walls and moat, tightened watch posts, patrolled regularly, and made the defenses complete.

sentences.zh: 按行鄉鄙，舉團練，立砦十有九，枹鼓相聞，久之得步卒萬八千、騎士三百。

translations.literal: He toured the countryside, raised militia training, established nineteen stockades with drums and gongs within hearing of one another, and in time mustered eighteen thousand foot soldiers and three hundred cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He toured the countryside, organized militia, and established nineteen stockades whose drums could be heard from one to the next; in time he mustered eighteen thousand foot soldiers and three hundred cavalry.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史疏聞，令天鑑自治兵。

translations.literal: The touring censor memorialized the throne, and Tianjian was ordered to raise troops on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: The touring censor reported to the throne, and Tianjian was authorized to raise troops on his own.

sentences.zh: 廉得境內賊渠數輩，夜突至其鄉呼之出，賊錯愕不能遁，皆誅之。

translations.literal: He investigated and found several bandit chiefs within the district; by night he burst into their villages and called them out; the bandits, startled, could not escape and were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: He identified several bandit chiefs in the district, burst into their villages by night and called them out; caught off guard, they could not escape and were all executed.

sentences.zh: 寇據曹縣，巡撫檄天鑑與諸道兵會剿，率所部為前鋒，冒矢石深入，諸軍踵之，復其城。

translations.literal: Bandits held Cao County; the governor ordered Tianjian to join circuit troops in suppression; he led his own men as vanguard, braved arrows and stones in a deep advance, the other armies followed, and the city was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits seized Cao County the governor ordered Tianjian to join circuit troops in a joint campaign; he led his men as vanguard, advanced under fire, the main force followed, and the city was recovered.

sentences.zh: 嘗以輕騎逐賊，日暮被圍，短兵相接，手格殺數賊，潰圍出，不失一騎。

translations.literal: Once with light cavalry he pursued bandits; at dusk he was surrounded; at close quarters he killed several bandits with his own hands, broke out, and did not lose a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: Once with a light cavalry detachment he pursued bandits; at dusk he was surrounded, fought hand to hand, killed several with his own blade, broke out, and did not lose a single horse.

sentences.zh: 在恩四年，屢與寇戰，俘馘無算，降者安撫之。

translations.literal: During four years at En he fought bandits repeatedly, took countless prisoners and heads, and pacified those who surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In four years at En he fought bandits repeatedly, took countless prisoners and heads, and pacified those who surrendered.

sentences.zh: 寇遠遁，招徠屯種，流亡復歸，墾荒千八百頃。

translations.literal: The bandits fled far away; he summoned people to settle and farm; the displaced returned; one thousand eight hundred qing of wasteland were opened.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits fled far away he encouraged settlement and farming; refugees returned and eighteen hundred qing of wasteland were brought under cultivation.

sentences.zh: 建書院，弦誦不輟。

translations.literal: He built an academy; the sound of study never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He founded an academy where the sound of study never ceased.

sentences.zh: 政聲為山東最，上考，內遷禮部主事。

translations.literal: His reputation in office was the foremost in Shandong; on superior evaluation he was transferred within the capital to a secretary in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation was the finest in Shandong; rated top in evaluation, he was transferred to the capital as a secretary in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十一年，始行耤田親耕禮，天鑑參酌古今，悉合禮宜。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the ritual of the emperor's personal plowing at the sacred field was first performed; Tianjian weighed ancient and modern precedents and all accorded with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the emperor first performed the sacred-field plowing ritual in person; Tianjian weighed ancient and modern precedents and arranged everything in proper ritual form.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to director.

sentences.zh: 主山東鄉試。

translations.literal: He presided over the Shandong provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Shandong provincial civil examination.

sentences.zh: 十二年，出為陝西河西道參議。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he went out to serve as assistant administrator of the Hexi circuit in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was posted as assistant administrator of the Hexi circuit in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 與屬吏約，毋獵民枉法。

translations.literal: He agreed with his subordinates not to hunt the people or bend the law.
translations.idiomatic: He pledged to his staff that they would not prey on the people or pervert the law.

sentences.zh: 天鑑固長治兵，按籍討軍實，誡將弁毋以軍糈肥私橐。

translations.literal: Tianjian was skilled in governing troops; he checked registers to verify military strength and warned officers not to fatten private purses with army grain.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjian was skilled at military administration; he audited registers to verify troop strength and warned officers not to line their pockets with army grain.

sentences.zh: 性剛介負氣，數忤上官。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and proud; he often offended his superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and proud by nature, he often clashed with his superiors.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，謝病歸。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year he resigned on grounds of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 絕跡公府，門下士或有餽遺，不受，曰：「飭簠簋，惜名節，足以報舉主矣！

translations.literal: He kept away from government offices; when disciples sometimes offered gifts he would not accept them, saying: "To keep my vessels pure and cherish my reputation is enough to repay my patron!
translations.idiomatic: He kept away from official life; when disciples offered gifts he refused them, saying, "Keeping my conduct pure and my reputation intact is repayment enough to those who recommended me!

sentences.zh: 」康熙初，大臣薦，不出。

translations.literal: " In early Kangxi ministers recommended him, but he would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: " In early Kangxi ministers recommended him, but he would not return to office.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long after.

sentences.zh: =趙廷標=趙廷標，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: =Zhao Tingbiao= Zhao Tingbiao was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tingbiao came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，以拔貢生授福建永定知縣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, as a selected tribute student he was appointed magistrate of Yongding in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shunzhi, as a selected tribute student he was appointed magistrate of Yongding in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 廣東大埔逸寇江龍以萬餘人犯縣城，廷標城守。

translations.literal: The fugitive bandit Jiang Long of Dabu in Guangdong invaded the county seat with more than ten thousand men; Tingbiao defended the city.
translations.idiomatic: The fugitive bandit Jiang Long of Dabu in Guangdong attacked the county seat with more than ten thousand men; Tingbiao held the walls.

sentences.zh: 寇穴地入，瀦池水以待，地砲不得發；

translations.literal: The bandits tunneled in; he dammed pool water to wait for them, so the land mines could not be fired;
translations.idiomatic: The bandits tunneled under the walls; he dammed pool water to flood them, so the land mines could not be fired;

sentences.zh: 樹雲梯乘城，於城上懸柵墮之。

translations.literal: they raised cloud ladders to scale the wall; he hung barriers from the wall to drop on them.
translations.idiomatic: they raised scaling ladders; he hung barriers from the parapet to drop on them.

sentences.zh: 持三月，食垂盡。

translations.literal: The siege lasted three months and food was nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted three months and food was nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 值立春，廷標張鼓樂，開城門，迎春東郊。

translations.literal: It was the Beginning of Spring; Tingbiao set out drums and music, opened the city gate, and welcomed spring in the eastern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: At the Beginning of Spring festival Tingbiao staged music, opened the gates, and went out to welcome spring in the eastern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 寇疑有伏，引去。

translations.literal: The bandits suspected an ambush and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits suspected an ambush and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 密遣兵間道往伏兩山間，出不意夾擊，敗之。

translations.literal: He secretly sent troops by a hidden path to lie in ambush between two mountains and struck them unexpectedly from both sides, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent troops by a hidden path to lie in ambush between two hills and struck them from both sides by surprise, defeating them.

sentences.zh: 進至龍磜寨，捕斬略盡。

translations.literal: Advancing to Longji Stockade, he captured and beheaded nearly all of them.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Longji Stockade, he captured and killed nearly all of them.

sentences.zh: 擢湖廣衡州同知，署府事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to sub-prefect of Hengzhou in Huguang and acted as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to sub-prefect of Hengzhou in Huguang and acted as prefect.

sentences.zh: 蠲賦墾荒，流亡復業。

translations.literal: He remitted taxes and opened wasteland; the displaced returned to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: He remitted taxes and encouraged reclamation; refugees returned to their fields.

sentences.zh: 歲大饑，賑恤有實惠。

translations.literal: In a year of great famine his relief brought real benefit.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine his relief brought real benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 經略大學士洪承疇薦廷標，十七年，擢雲南迤東道副使。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou, commissioner-general, recommended Tingbiao; in the seventeenth year he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Yidong circuit in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary and commissioner-general Hong Chengchou recommended Tingbiao; in the seventeenth year he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Yidong circuit in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 安普諸番為土官所誘，競作不靖。

translations.literal: The various tribes of Anpu, incited by native officials, vied in making trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes of Anpu, incited by native officials, rose in unrest one after another.

sentences.zh: 廷標設方略、行間，解散之，遂復維摩舊地。

translations.literal: Tingbiao devised strategy and sowed dissension among them, dispersed them, and thus recovered the old territory of Weimo.
translations.idiomatic: Tingbiao devised strategy and sowed dissension among them, broke up their forces, and recovered the old Weimo territory.

sentences.zh: 移檄諭寧州彌勒、巴盤、八甸，罷捕逐之令，令諸持田器者皆為良民，持兵者乃為賊。

translations.literal: He issued proclamations to instruct Ningzhou, Mile, Bapan, and Badian, abolished orders to hunt and drive people out, and declared that all who held farming tools were to be treated as good people, while only those who bore arms were bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He issued proclamations to Ningzhou, Mile, Bapan, and Badian, ending the orders to hunt people down, and ruled that anyone holding farming tools was a law-abiding subject while only those bearing arms were bandits.

sentences.zh: 巡行安撫，諸路悉平。

translations.literal: He toured the region to pacify it, and all routes were entirely settled.
translations.idiomatic: He toured the region to pacify it, and every route was brought to peace.

sentences.zh: 治迤東十八年。

translations.literal: He governed Yidong for eighteen years.
translations.idiomatic: He held office in Yidong for eighteen years.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，調廣東廣肇南韶道副使。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign he was transferred to be vice commissioner of the Guangzhaonanxiao circuit in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kangxi era he was transferred to vice commissioner of the Guangzhaonanxiao circuit in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 安普民、蠻聞其去，塹道塞城留之。

translations.literal: When the people and tribes of Anpu heard he was leaving, they dug ditches across the roads and blocked the city to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: When the people and tribes of Anpu learned he was leaving, they dug ditches across the roads and blocked the city gates to keep him.

sentences.zh: 慰諭再三，乃得行。

translations.literal: After repeated consolation and instruction he was able to depart.
translations.idiomatic: Only after repeated appeals could he finally depart.

sentences.zh: 兩粵八排諸山寇聞廷標來，望風解散。

translations.literal: When the mountain bandits of the Eight Ranks in the two Guang provinces heard Tingbiao was coming, they dispersed at the mere rumor of his approach.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain bandits of the Eight Ranks in the two Guang provinces heard Tingbiao was coming and melted away before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 連州亂，至，立就撫。

translations.literal: Lianzhou was in revolt; when he arrived, they immediately submitted to pacification.
translations.idiomatic: When Lianzhou rose in revolt, he arrived and the rebels submitted at once.

sentences.zh: 逾年以憂去。

translations.literal: After more than a year he left on bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year he went home to mourn.

sentences.zh: 起湖南驛鹽道副使。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as vice commissioner of the courier and salt circuit in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning, he was appointed vice commissioner of the courier and salt circuit in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 捕治劇寇，誅其渠，餘悉縱歸農。

translations.literal: He captured and punished fierce bandits, executed their chiefs, and released the rest to return to farming.
translations.idiomatic: He captured fierce bandits, executed their leaders, and sent the rest back to their fields.

sentences.zh: 湖南方用兵，芻茭械仗，儲峙供給，不誤晷刻，民不困役。

translations.literal: Hunan was then at war; fodder, weapons, and equipment were stockpiled and supplied without missing a moment, and the people were not worn down by corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan was at war; he stockpiled fodder and arms and met every deadline without burdening the people with corvée.

sentences.zh: 兼攝糧道。

translations.literal: He also acted as grain commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He also served concurrently as grain commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會湘東民變，巡撫韓世琦令廷標往撫之。

translations.literal: When the people of eastern Hunan rose in revolt, Governor Han Shiqi ordered Tingbiao to go and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When eastern Hunan erupted in unrest, Governor Han Shiqi ordered Tingbiao to go and pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 單騎馳諭，皆悔泣聽命，散遣之。

translations.literal: He rode alone in haste to instruct them; all repented, wept, and obeyed, and he dispersed them.
translations.idiomatic: He rode out alone to reason with them; they wept in repentance, obeyed, and were sent home.

sentences.zh: 事稍定，修岳麓書院，置田禀諸生。

translations.literal: When affairs had settled somewhat, he restored the Yuelu Academy and set aside fields to support the students.
translations.idiomatic: When order returned he restored Yuelu Academy and endowed fields to support its students.

sentences.zh: 嘗行部至衡州，父老羅拜車下，號以「慈母」。

translations.literal: Once when touring his jurisdiction he reached Hengzhou; elders lined up to bow beneath his carriage and called him the "kind mother."
translations.idiomatic: Once while on circuit at Hengzhou, elders lined the road to bow before his carriage and hailed him as their "kind mother."

sentences.zh: 俄遷陝西糧儲道參議。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be assistant administrator of the grain storage circuit in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to assistant administrator of the grain storage circuit in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 已病，值武昌兵變，軍書至，猶強起視事。

translations.literal: He was already ill; when the military mutiny at Wuchang broke out and dispatches arrived, he still forced himself to rise and attend to business.
translations.idiomatic: Already ill, when the Wuchang mutiny broke out and military dispatches arrived, he still forced himself to attend to business.

sentences.zh: 病篤乞歸，至家卒。

translations.literal: His illness grew grave and he begged to return home; he died upon reaching his house.
translations.idiomatic: His illness worsened and he begged leave to go home; he died soon after arriving.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：自置督撫，而兩司權輕，況於各道；

translations.literal: =Commentary= The commentary says: Since governors-general and governors were established, the two provincial commissioners have held lighter authority, to say nothing of circuit officials;
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Since governors-general and governors were established, the two provincial commissioners have held lighter authority, to say nothing of circuit officials;

sentences.zh: 然以賢者處之，奉職循理，視民之所急，弭亂解嬈，亦足以為治。

translations.literal: yet when men of worth hold such posts, fulfilling duty and following principle, looking to what the people urgently need, quelling disorder and relieving distress, that too is sufficient for good government.
translations.idiomatic: yet when worthy men hold such posts, fulfill their duties, heed what the people urgently need, and quell disorder and relieve distress, that too is enough to govern well.

sentences.zh: 而述、振芬、振姬、天鑑皆有才略，根本尤在廉勤。

translations.literal: Ershu, Zhenfen, Zhenji, and Tianjian all had talent and strategy; the root lay especially in integrity and diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Ershu, Zhenfen, Zhenji, and Tianjian all had talent and strategic ability; the foundation of their success lay above all in integrity and diligence.

sentences.zh: 延著、國棟、廷標當治亂用重之日，濟之以寬仁，雖以是罷貶，甚或中危法，而一不自卹，是皆能舉其職者。

translations.literal: Yanzhu, Guodong, and Tingbiao, in days when order and disorder called for stern measures, supplemented rule with leniency and kindness; though for this some were dismissed or demoted, and some even fell under deadly law, yet none spared himself—these were all men who could fulfill their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhu, Guodong, and Tingbiao served in an age that demanded stern measures yet tempered rule with mercy; though some were dismissed or demoted, and some even faced capital punishment, none held back for his own sake—all fulfilled their duties.

sentences.zh: 澤及於斯民，亦已多矣。

translations.literal: The benefit reaching these people was already very great.
translations.idiomatic: The good they did for the people was already very great indeed.
